item.description:
What's new in 1.4.0

  • A new look, and a setup you can follow. One light, calm design across every window, the menu and both bars. Setup shows what to do on the left and a live picture on the right, and opens Home with your words, time saved and streak. Updates install in one click. History looks like a place you want to be. A header shows your week — words, time saved, streak and the last two weeks as bars — and dictations sit on a timeline grouped by day: the time, your words in big type, the app they went into as its real icon, and your voice as you spoke it, as long as the dictation was. Point at a row for copy, insert again, transcribe again and delete; a click opens the whole text, and copying says “Copied” right on the row. Move with ↑ and ↓, insert with ⏎, copy with ⌘C, open with Space and search with ⌘F. Show only what needs attention, and scroll through thousands of entries without a stall. Screenshots and Recordings use the same timeline. Setup ends on your three keys: Dictation, Screenshot and Recording, exactly as you set them. While you sign in in the browser there is now a “Cancel” if you closed the tab, “Skip this one” no longer sits on the last test where it did nothing, and the text in the plan and checkout reads cleaner.
  • Recordings have a pause. Thinking? Pause from the bar or the notch — the clock stops, the bar turns amber, and nothing is recorded until you resume. Stop is never red now: red only means recording. Recordings are ready the moment you stop. They are saved instantly and ready for your agent within about a second — a 9-minute recording took 8 minutes in 1.3.1. Cueshot keeps every screen that mattered, ties each sentence you say to what was on screen, and your agent gets a timeline, one overview image and search over the text. Recordings are about a quarter of the size.
  • Your agent can ask you out loud. When it needs a decision, a large card grows from the notch — the agent with its icon, the folder, how long it will still wait (“closes in 64 s”), and the question in big type with what you can say — and waits until you have finished dictating, recording or whatever else is on the notch, then shows up a second later — several questions come one after the other, none is lost. A band under the agent shows what is happening: reading aloud, your turn, listening, sending, sent. Click an option and it goes out at once (with the pointer over the card, 1 to 4 and ⏎ work too, and nothing is typed into your editor); when several can be right, your agent lets you tick as many as you like and confirm with Send or ⏎. Or press your dictation key to hear it, just talk, press it again to send — your words are recognized exactly like a dictation, your word list included, and nothing you say is shown. Clicked and spoken go out together. If you take a screenshot, start a recording or dictate while a question is open, it steps aside and comes back when you are done; fn waits until the microphone is really on, and the card says “Starting microphone…” while it starts. Esc puts it off until later. It waits 3 minutes (up to 5 while you are busy, and at least 90 seconds once it is on screen), then 90 seconds after your last move — nobody who is reading, answering or sending is cut off (5 minutes at most), and what you said or ticked still goes out. If you haven't noticed it, it knocks again after 20 and 60 seconds, and a dot on the menu bar icon stays while a question waits. If nobody answers, your agent is told whether you were busy or away, and told not to decide for you or do anything hard to undo: it asks in the chat and waits. The short note Cueshot adds to your agents' instruction files (less than a third of the length it had) is refreshed only when its wording changes, and if you delete it yourself it stays deleted.
  • One clean handover to your agent. Everything in the bundle goes over once, the next screenshot starts a fresh bundle, and the notch says who got it. After a screenshot or a recording the notch also offers Copy (the picture, to paste anywhere) and Copy for agent (the sentence that points your agent at it). Remove single items in the Bundle window; "look at my last capture" always finds the one you just took. Marks you draw on a screenshot or during a recording are numbered 1, 2, 3 — on the picture and in what your agent reads — so you can say “point 2”. Keys and passwords stay out of it: an API key, token, private key or password in a web address that was on your screen or in what you said reaches your agent as [redacted] (pictures are shown as they are, and your agent is told when something was hidden), and text read from your screen is marked as something to read, not a command to follow. Shortcuts no longer step on each other: inserting the last screenshot (hold left ⌘, tap right ⌘) or the bundle hint (hold left ⌘, tap right ⌥) show the picture they stand for, small, in the notch, and the screenshot one also puts your clipboard back afterwards, ignores a second press, never covers a dictation or an open question with “inserted”, and says “deleted” instead of slipping in an older picture when you removed the last one from History. Starting a recording under an open screenshot area, or re-inserting a dictation in the middle of a new one, is ignored. Your keys follow one rule: the key you capture with pastes it while you hold left ⌘. Screenshot is a double tap of right ⌘ and Recording a double tap of right ⌥ (the left sides trigger nothing — tap one twice and Cueshot says to use the right), so hold left ⌘ and tap right ⌘ for the last screenshot, right ⌥ for the sentence that sends your agent to the bundle or your last recording, and fn for the last dictation once more (a dictation that is running is never interrupted). If you change a key, its paste grip moves with it; where it can't (left ⌘, both sides, a key combination) Settings → Shortcuts shows what applies instead (⌃⌥V, ⌃⌥B, ⌃⌥D) and lets you choose. The grip works in either order, and Settings → Shortcuts, the menu and setup say exactly what to press. Setup lets you try the paste grips; if you had kept the old factory keys (⌘⌘, ⌥⌥, ⌃ held, ⌃V) they move to the new ones once, and anything you chose yourself stays.
  • Dictation you can see. Tap fn and the notch opens at once; tap again and it changes — a turning ring, “Transcribing…” or “Cleaning up…”, the waveform folding into dots — before the text lands. On the Free plan the notch always says “Mini model” in amber; on Pro it shows only your voice — the waveform follows how loudly and how softly you speak — and says so when it falls back to the Mini model. Dictation you can press again right away. Pro recognizes in the cloud by default and fixes names from your word list — about five times fewer mistakes than on-device in our tests. Soft words are kept, text arrives sooner, and if the server is slow your Mac takes over within seconds (a brief network hiccup gets one retry first). If your microphone sends nothing, the notch says “No sound from” and the name of your microphone instead of leaving you to talk to nobody — and with Bluetooth headphones that deliver only silence, Cueshot rebuilds the audio path by itself. Nothing is lost quietly any more: if the cloud hears no word, your Mac listens once more; and when your voice was in the recording but no words came out, the recording stays in History with “Transcribe again”. On the Free plan, your word list holds up better: “Cueshot” is always on it and can’t be removed by accident, the mini model no longer turns “the cursor” into “The Cursor” or “gibt” into “Git”, and a word you add works in the very next dictation. In setup, the dictation step now shows whatever was recognized and moves on. Dictation no longer invents words such as “Thank you”, “Yeah” or “Okay” out of room noise: stretches of sound without a voice in them are skipped before anything listens to them (Mini and Pro alike), and on Pro a cleanup that tacks a greeting or a thank-you onto your sentence, or cuts most of a long sentence away, is ignored. And when a dictation doesn't land — you switched apps, there was no text field, you pressed esc, it took too long — the notch now says so and tells you the keys that bring it back (“Not inserted — app changed. Hold ⌘ left, tap fn to insert it.”), follows your own shortcut if you changed it, and the text is the one that key inserts next (the notch says “Inserted” the first time); no dialog pops up over it any more.
  • Your agent can watch any video. It analyses a video or audio file on your Mac like one of your recordings — every screen, its text and a transcript, faster than real time, free, nothing uploaded — and it always knows what it can ask of Cueshot.
  • Agents feel at home. Say "at readme dot md" and your agent gets @README.md; Cursor gets its instructions in one paste; MCP servers that need an account now have "Sign in".
  • Your agent can prepare a message or files for a friend — but it can never send: a card in the notch shows who gets what and how big it is, and only you send it (⏎) or discard it (esc). Drafts wait 24 hours, and a dot on the menu bar icon says one is waiting. <!-- freunde -->
  • Accounts only when you need one. Free never needs an account; sign in for Pro. Pro is €4.99 a month. Pay for Pro right in the app — pick a plan, type your card in a secure field that goes straight to Stripe (Cueshot never sees it), and Pro is on the moment it goes through — and manage it there too: “Pro until 5 Nov — won't renew”, cancel or withdraw with a confirmation that shows the exact time we received it, switch plans, change your card, and open every invoice — numbered, with its PDF, and marked “Refunded” once you withdraw. Not signed in yet? Choose a plan and sign in right there with Google, Apple or email; payment opens by itself afterwards, and if you already pay, you land in your subscription instead of a second checkout.
  • Invite friends and earn a month of Pro. Copy your personal link, share it from the macOS share menu, or open a ready message in your mail app — you read it and send it yourself, from your own address; Cueshot sends no email for you. For every friend who starts paying for Pro after their free week, you get one month of Pro as credit on your next invoice — up to twelve months. The terms are one click away. <!-- empfehlung -->
  • Friends who get your things right away, end-to-end encrypted. You're connected once you've both added each other: someone who added you shows up in Friends as a request with “Accept” — at once when you open Friends, otherwise within a few minutes — and until they add you back you can add them but not send — the row says so. Sending is part of Pro; receiving is free. Then send them files, recorded videos (shrunk to fit if they're big), bundles and messages from Friends, from the Send button in the notch after a screenshot or recording, or by dropping a file on the menu bar icon. What arrives lands as a card that grows from the notch — with a picture of the screenshot or the recording's first frame, the sender, the size, and the buttons that fit: Copy puts the picture on your clipboard, Copy for agent gives your agent one sentence that leads it to exactly this item, Save puts it in Downloads, Open opens it (keys C, A, S and ⏎ once you click the card). It shows up within about half a minute (up to two minutes once their Mac has sat untouched for five minutes, up to five when the screen is locked or the Mac has sat untouched for an hour — and the moment they are back) — never in the middle of a dictation, a recording, a screenshot or a question from your agent: it waits and comes right after, as one note (“Tim · 2 new things”), and a dot on the menu bar icon and the sidebar stays until you've looked. Screenshots and recordings from friends also sit in your Screenshots and Recordings pages under “From friends”, and your agent can read them — it is told what each one is. A file from a friend is never opened for you unless it is a picture, video, sound, text or PDF, and it is never written to Downloads until you press Save. Sending is lighter, too: text is compressed before it is encrypted, big files go up in parts and only the missing part is repeated if the connection drops, a ring in the notch shows the progress, the same thing sent to another friend isn't uploaded again, and a recording can go as “Compact” — the text of every screen, the overview pages and the transcript, about ten times smaller than the video. You can remove a friend, decline a request or cancel an invite from Friends — the other person isn't told, and anything not yet picked up is deleted. Only safe things travel: apps, installers, scripts that run when opened, documents with macros, shortcuts and anything disguised as a picture are refused before they leave your Mac and again on the Mac that receives them, before anything is saved; archives Cueshot can't look into are marked “not checked”, and source code arrives as plain text that is never opened or run. <!-- freunde --> The list stays up to date while you look at it. With the Friends window open, the list checks for news every 15 seconds — you see "Connected" or a new request without closing and reopening it. "Send to" asks for the current list before it opens, so a friend who just signed out is no longer offered. And if a send fails because a friend signed out or removed you, the app now says so in one sentence and refreshes the list at once. <!-- freunde-frisch -->
  • The legal texts are one click away: Settings → Updates → Legal opens the privacy policy and the terms, and “Open-source licenses” shows the licenses and credits of everything Cueshot is built on (NVIDIA Parakeet, pyannote, Sparkle and more) — from a file on your Mac, so it works offline. Two lines in the app now say what our server keeps and what the AI providers may keep, and the “5× fewer errors” now says it is from our test. Usage counts and error reports are now off until you turn them on: setup asks (nothing pre-selected), and if you said yes before, “What's new” asks once more — errors and crashes are now part of it, without ever sending what a message said.
  • Dictation understands when you correct yourself and when you list. On Pro, “let's meet at three, no, at four” becomes “let's meet at four” (also “ich meine”, “scratch that”, “actually”), and “erstens … zweitens …” or “first … second …” in one sentence becomes a numbered list — and when nothing was corrected, your words stay exactly as you said them.
  • The notch stays where it should. After days of running, a long sleep or a screen change, it could end up behind a full-screen window or not show at all; now it checks itself every time it appears and puts itself back — and if it ever has to, it writes down what was wrong. The frame you drag for a screenshot checks itself the same way, even over a full-screen app: if it can't take your click it brings itself forward, rebuilds, or closes and says so. Esc cancels a screenshot — even while another app is in front. It never stops or discards a recording; a trash button in the recording bar does that, after one question. Switching between full-screen apps and Spaces no longer moves it for nothing.
  • Mute your microphone while recording. One button in the recording bar and in the notch — struck through and amber when muted: the picture keeps going, your voice is left out of the video, the text and the sound, and your agent reads “Microphone muted 01:10–01:42”. Dictating with fn, or answering your agent's question out loud, during a recording mutes it for you.
  • The notch tells you what your agent took. “Claude Code · cueshot took 2 screenshots”, “… took the recording”, “… took the bundle (3 items)” — once, together when it takes several, never in the middle of dictating, recording or a question. Something your agent fetches on its own — the last screenshot, say — leaves the bundle, so it never gets it twice.
